speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues; to begin our assessment, have these symptoms been present continuously or do they come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's disease (likely Parkinson's Plus Syndrome such as Progressive Supranuclear Palsy or Dementia with Lewy Bodies).
I see a 70-year-old man with a one-year history of progressive unilateral hand tremor and recent memory decline affecting instrumental activities like paying bills. Since the tremor has been present for a year before the memory issues began, I need to clarify if he is currently taking any medications and if he has noticed any changes in his balance or gait recently. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Metanephrines (to rule out Pheochromocytoma).
